idea.Name: a2_prasc_validation_quantitative_audit
idea.Title: Quantitative Audit and Falsification Report for A2 Rank, Bias, and Acquisition Controls
idea.Short Hypothesis: The existing a2val E1/E2/E3/E5 and optional physical-tangent artifacts can be converted into a substantive quantitative validation report by adding fixed-seed replication, uncertainty estimates, baseline comparisons, and interpretation of the previously generated result files. No new algorithm, model, or hardware claim is introduced.
idea.Related Work: Projections, Schur complements, SOM/TSOM, coherent calibration, variable projection, source extension, continuation, and experiment design remain prior machinery. Idriss and Raj arXiv2503.07316 already jointly calibrate complex factors in multifrequency SOM. The existing implementation produced an a2val package, run scripts, tests, JSON/CSV results, and figures; this revision is an analysis and reporting pass over those artifacts rather than a new method proposal.
idea.Abstract: We revise the A2 validation work package into a written quantitative audit. The implemented E1/E2/E3/E5 modules and the optional shared physical-core tangent run are rerun under a fixed seed matrix with recorded Monte Carlo sample sizes. Their JSON/CSV outputs are parsed into normalized evidence tables for backward-error-scaled identity residuals, Fisher contraction, covariance/bias risk, and acquisition innovation. Planned baseline comparisons are executed and reported: physical versus free-current envelope, relative-only versus absolute and bias-aware gates, shared-map versus independent-map profiling, and greedy versus pair lookahead. Negative controls, threshold sweeps, replication variability, and counterexamples are documented. The conclusion is limited to whether the conditional controls hold, fail, or remain indeterminate on synthetic examples; this revision does not claim nonlinear superiority, SOM exclusivity, hardware success, or full-plan completion.

datasets: Existing A2 E1 scalar matched complex/intensity exact examples
Existing A2 E2/E3/E5 exact and random fixed-tangent examples under a fixed seed matrix
Optional physical tangents from the separately implemented shared core, interpreted only as secondary corroboration
Negative-control and threshold-sweep outputs generated from the existing a2val modules
baselines: relative-only versus absolute and bias-aware gates
metrics: backward-error-scaled identity residual mean, standard deviation, and 95% confidence interval across seeds
Fisher contraction ratio with Monte Carlo confidence intervals
covariance and bias risk ratios versus absolute and relative gates
acquisition innovation gain, submodularity violation count, and policy delta
Experiments.compute_estimate: Small CPU-only NumPy/SciPy using the existing venv and generated artifacts. Add one seed-matrix rerun/table-writer script and rerun existing E1-E5/physical scripts. No GPU, no installation, no new large-scale data.
steps: Read research/delegated/a2_theory_validation/TASK.md and parse all existing results/*.json and results/*_summary.csv into a single evidence view
Add a fixed seed-matrix runner for E1, E2, E3, E5, and the optional physical tangent, recording seed count, Monte Carlo sample size, and runtime
Compute normalized identity/control residuals with backward-error scaling, confidence intervals, and Fisher contraction metrics from the reruns
Execute and report the four planned baseline comparisons, preserving raw JSON/CSV and generating compact tables
Run negative controls and threshold sweeps from existing modules; classify false-positive modes and rank/noise threshold sensitivity
Write a concise quantitative Results and Replication supplement with tables, figures, and explicit positive/negative/indeterminate conclusions
Preserve all discrepancies and counterexamples; do not claim E4, publication acceptance, universal basin, or hardware success

Risk Factors and Limitations: The synthetic validation package may still be too small or underpowered for a full ACL Rolling Review paper even after quantitative reporting
Identities may be model conditional, and passing synthetic tangent tests does not imply nonlinear method superiority
Noise, realification, and rank thresholds can create false positives; negative controls are reported to bound this risk
The optional physical-tangent run is only secondary corroboration and may be too weak for strong conclusions
Do not resume stale geometry-lift claims or overstate the reach of conditional validation evidence

report.summary: This round completed the requested analysis-only quantitative audit of the existing A2 validation package. It did not re-run the underlying E1/E2/E3/E5 or physical-optional experiments; instead it confirmed the directory state, parsed all existing summary CSVs and raw JSON artifacts, extracted numeric evidence, computed seed-level 95% Student-t confidence intervals, ran the existing assertion test suite, checked the results against the preregistered protocol, and wrote human- and machine-readable deliverables. The audit substantiates the conditional synthetic rank/bias/acquisition controls and records explicit gaps without claiming E4, nonlinear superiority, SOM exclusivity, or publication acceptance.
key_results: Test suite passed 50/50 assertion checks with all runners exiting 0: E1 9/9, E2 11/11, E3 15/15, E5 14/14, physical smoke 1/1.

E1: matched contraction J_ph <= J_coh held in all four scalar models; known-reference case gave J_coh=2.0 and J_ph=0.5258 analytically versus 2.003 and 0.5285 empirically, with empirical-minus-analytic 95% CIs containing zero; mismatch control reversed ordering by design (J_mismatch=1960 vs J_coh=2).

E2: loss identity residual was 0; rank drops were exact (0/0, 1/1, 2/2); rho nonmonotonicity reproduced [0.75, 1.0, 1.55e-15]; T5b passed 36/36; max backward-scaled residual was 0.2734 (<100); saturation J_x_fro was 7.0e-16 (scaled 0.0971); [1,1e-8,1e-14,0] yielded rank 2 and never rank 4.

E3: dual spectra were exact; K_e <= K_eL <= K0 held; Theorem-7 risk was 9.418 = 3.1997 variance + 6.2183 bias^2; Monte Carlo stayed within 3 SE on 10/10 seeds with max relative error 4.1% variance and 5.3% bias; covariance relative mean was 0.0576; relative-only and residual-only gates failed high-bias cases.

E5: shared-map J_stack=2 exceeded sum_J=0; duplicate frame residual was ~1e-15; budget identity passed 24/24 (max 2.34e-14); 0/24 random rank enlargements satisfied I>=L and all correctly degraded J; crafted compensate/non-compensate and neutral controls behaved as predicted; greedy logdet was 8.0418 versus exhaustive 8.1263 (gap 0.0845); non-submodularity gaps were 3.04 and 7.60; gauge null persisted and anchor restored it.

Physical optional run was interpreted only as secondary corroboration: phase0/1/2 passed; T5b 24/24; max T5a scaled residual 0.01006; Theorem-3 residual 3.17e-11; innovation relative error 4.48e-16; stack>=sum passed 12/12. Theorem 7 skipped 12/12 because the declared C1 saturated the visible pose direction, making B_v numerically zero.

Computed 95% CIs across recorded seeds for E1 Fisher means, E2 36 tangent residuals, E3 Theorem-7 MC relative errors, E5 24 budget-identity residuals, and physical phase1/phase2 aggregates; outputs are in results/ci_stats.json and results/ci_stats.txt.

Honest gaps were preserved: E1 physical full-wave Fisher scene, E3 limited-aperture tangents, E3 nearly-parallel-range control, E5 physical 8-candidate acquisition-policy comparison, E5 source-stabilizer control, E4 primary comparison, and publication evidence boundary were not run and are not claimed.

dead_ends: No failed runs or algorithm bugs occurred in this round.

No new fixed-seed runner was added because the existing scripts already record protocol seed ranges (101-110, 201-212, 301-310, 401-412) and sample sizes; the only missing datum, synthetic wall time, was disclosed rather than fabricated.
The E5 physical-policy ledger row initially appeared to attribute the synthetic-only policy comparison to the physical run; this was corrected during verification.

unresolved_issues: The planned fixed-seed matrix rerun was not actually executed; CIs were computed from previously recorded seeds, so true replication variability, Monte Carlo sample sizes, runtimes, and independent-seed robustness are not established.

The four planned baseline comparisons were not run as new first-class experiments; they were only parsed from existing summary artifacts, so no new controlled ablation tables or raw JSON/CSV evidence were generated.

Negative controls, threshold sweeps, false-positive mode classification, and counterexample summaries were not run as planned; these are necessary to bound the risk of synthetic test artifacts and to show the controls are not merely vacuous identity checks.

The evidence is concentrated on exact/random synthetic scalar and tangent examples; there is no broader sweep across noise levels, rank thresholds, model configurations, or feasible additional settings/datasets, so it is too thin for a full ACL Rolling Review paper.

Several preregistered gaps remain untested, including E4 primary comparison, limited-aperture tangents, the nearly-parallel-range control, and the physical 8-candidate acquisition-policy comparison; these omissions prevent substantive full-paper conclusions.

The report is largely a validation supplement documenting conditional sanity checks and exact identities; it does not yet provide the substantive empirical contribution, ablations, or robustness/sensitivity analyses expected of a full-length top-venue paper.
verdict.reasoning: The audit did produce a clean, internally consistent summary: 50/50 assertions passed, several identities matched analytic expectations, and gaps were honestly disclosed. However, the experiment report explicitly states it did not re-run the underlying experiments and instead parsed existing artifacts. That means the central empirical claims are not supported by new independent replication, the planned baseline comparisons and negative controls were not executed, and the study remains a pilot-level validation of a synthetic package rather than a thoroughly established full-paper contribution. The positive results are mostly conditional identity/sanity checks with zero or near-zero residuals, and the absence of threshold sweeps, broader settings, and key preregistered comparisons leaves too many unresolved issues for a top-venue full-length paper. The core idea of a quantitative audit remains worth keeping, but it must be deepened substantially before writing up.
